evals.prompt: Critique this design doc before I circulate it to the team. [design doc: a TL;DR full of adjectives, an approach section that says 'industry standard', no SLOs, and a one-line rollout plan]
assertions: Every finding quotes the document verbatim rather than paraphrasing it — the quoted snippet is the audit trail
Findings are local and anchored to a section, not global judgments like 'the tone is off'
Severity is calibrated — blockers do not outnumber majors
Fixes are paste-able: when the fix is 'add a section', the critique shows what that section should contain
The critique reviews whether the doc made its case, and does not re-debate the underlying technical topic
The document archetype is identified and the critique is run against that archetype's quality bar

evals.prompt: This exec summary (exec-summary.md) goes in Fernhill's board pack on Friday. The pack limit is two pages and it's already at two, so I can't add anything. Just tell me what to fix - don't rewrite it for me.
assertions: Catches that the phase totals (140 + 120 + 62 = 322) do not match the 312 homes stated
Challenges the 40% bill-cut claim as unsupported by a six-home pilot measured over one summer month
Spots that the January 2027 start contradicts the contractor being unable to start before April 2027
Notes that the summary never says what decision it needs from the board, or by when
Points each problem to where it sits in the document, by section or quoted text
Respects the length limit: fixes cut or replace existing text rather than only adding material, and the reply does not hand back a rewritten document
Does not invent figures or facts not in the document, such as a corrected savings figure

evals.prompt:
I'm on the committee of my son's under-11s football club and someone drafted this letter to parents about subs going up. I'm not a writer - can you just give me the top 3 problems with it?

"Dear Parents,

As you know, costs have been rising. From next season, subs will go from £120 to £150, a small 15% rise. Please pay by the end of the month via the usual method. We know this is a lot but we are sure you will understand.

Thanks,
The Committee"
assertions: Gives three problems, as asked, not a longer list
Catches that £120 to £150 is a 25% rise, not 15%
Each problem comes with a concrete fix the committee could make
Uses plain language suited to a parent volunteer
Does not invent facts about the club, such as its actual costs, a payment date or a payment method
